title: Values produced by the search construction
statement: Let $n,j\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a Boolean assignment to the $n$ input bits, and for each $r\in\mathbb{N}$ let $D_r$ be a Boolean circuit on $n+r$ inputs in which every gate has distinct arguments, every negation gate has exactly one argument, and every gate has at most two arguments. Define $b_0$ to be the empty list and, for $r\ge1$, define $b_r$ by appending to $b_{r-1}$ the value of $D_r$ on the input consisting of $x$, the bits of $b_{r-1}$, and a final true bit. Evaluating the gates of the search construction after $j$ stages on $x$, the value at vertex $n$ is true, and the values at its listed output vertices, in order, are exactly $b_j$.
hypotheses_covered: Each $D_r$ has distinct arguments at every gate
Each negation gate of $D_r$ has exactly one argument
Each gate of $D_r$ has at most two arguments
$x$ is a Boolean assignment to the $n$ input bits
